newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.N. to probe burning of Moslem refugee homes.
newsitem.headline: U.N. to probe burning of Moslem refugee homes.

text.p: The United Nations said on Friday it would investigate the burning of Moslem houses in Bosnian Serb territory after a Serb police investigation proved insufficient.
Over the past few weeks Serbs destroyed 15 houses belonging to Moslem refugees trying to resettle the village of Gajevi in Serb-controlled territory in northeastern Bosnia.
"It is clear to the U.N. that the investigation undertaken by the Republika Srpska police into the Gajevi incidents has been both tardy and inadequate," a U.N. international police spokesman said.
"Indeed, there are allegations, both direct and indirect, of local police force involvement," Liam McDowall said.
Gajevi is in the a former frontline area called the Zone of Separation (ZOS) between Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation and the Serb republic on the Serb side of the line.
Under the terms of Bosnia's peace accord, NATO is charged with patrolling the ZOS area. NATO said it is the local polices responsibility to uphold the law and order in each half of ZOS.
Serb president Biljana Plavsic promised recently an investigation into the house burnings, but results were inadequate, McDowall said.
Gajevi's pre-war Moslem residents hoped to follow an example of other three Moslem villages in the ZOS area, resettled last year under international supervision.
Serbs then began a campaign of night-time bombings last September, destroying dozens of houses in the ZOS area, where Moslems could possibly return and re-establish homes.
Refugees in Gajevi said they felt betrayed by NATO troops, whose presence gave them confidence to resettle.
